Just some commentary on this:
* the memory requirements are a bit prohibitive
* these tests really only cover the happy path
* the implementation tends to behave badly when faced with invalid input (e.g. invalid certificates, endless allocation failures, hanging, etc) 
* there needs to be more testing (ideally paired with fixes) for the non-happy path

This might be a good place to start though.

If there are any suggestions on reducing memory requirements please share them liberally - it would be nice to use TLS even on systems with less memory.

E.g. this works:
```
west build -b qemu_x86_64 -p always -t run tests/net/socket/tls
```
but this does not work (it just hangs on my machine.. no idea why. doesn't seem to run out of memory, but who knows :man_shrugging: )
```
west build -b mps2_an385 -p always -t run tests/net/socket/tls
```
I've also experienced a repeatable EIO when both ends of a TLS socket are attempting to write to it at the same time, but perhaps that is because it was locally connected.

issue_context.title: tests: sockets: tcp: add a tls test
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently I'm attempting to use mbedTLS in a custom application and am creating a test to verify TLS in CI. The test is multi-threaded and uses TCP sockets with the TLS extensions; the server server socket is managed by one thread and the client socket is managed by the main thread.

My reference(s) for the application were the `echo_server` / `echo_client` sample applications and I'm just using the certificates / keys from those sample applications as-is. However, I'm experiencing a handshake error in TLS.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It might be useful to have it a test that verified this kind of functionality in Zephyr CI

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Have looked around for existing tests that exercise this particular setup, but have found none.

**Additional context**
comments:
I used this patch to get a bit more detail from mbedTLS
[tls-debug.patch.txt](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/5731340/tls-debug.patch.txt)

review_comments:
You need to set the hostname, otherwise mbedTLS will reject the server certificate. The certificate from echo samples was issued for the `localhost` so the following will do the job:
```
setsockopt(client_fd, SOL_TLS, TLS_HOSTNAME, "localhost", sizeof("localhost"));
```
Hmm... if `CONFIG_NET_HOSTNAME_ENABLE` is not set, should a TLS example always fall back to "localhost" then? That could be one of the issues I was having with Greybus.

It has nothing to do with `CONFIG_NET_HOSTNAME_ENABLE` - `TLS_HOSTNAME` option specifies the name of the host for which the certificate was issued for (which is part of the certificate itslef, so called "Common Name"). When reaching some public server, it should match the hostname you connect to (see https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/samples/net/sockets/http_get/src/http_get.c#L105 for example).

Here, the certificates used by echo were created with Common Name set to `localhost`, so we need to use this name here.

It's also possible to skip hostname validation by explicitly setting this option to a NULL string, but it's isn't considered as safe practice.
K - not sure if all of the issues are fixed, but I added the `TLS_HOSTNAME`

Doesn't seem to be enough ram to run on `qemu_cortex_m3`

> Running my tests on `qemu_x86_64`, but the stack sizes needed here are enormous 8192 bytes for the client and server. I guess on `qemu_cortex_m3` that would probably only be 4096, but still.. a lot of resources.

Yes, mbedtls is a memory hog that requires lot of memory to function properly. Also you do not get nice information when running out of memory, things just fail in weird ways.

You can enable `CONFIG_STACK_SENTINEL` to detect stack overflows. The other issue looks like there's too little net bufs.

btw. You may expect delayed answers from my side, I started my christmas break today 🎄
After looking how `tests/net/socket/tcp` is doing things when connecting, I think you need to let other threads to run too, so `k_msleep()` might help here.
Good call. I was occasionally unable to connect and thought it may have been scheduler related, although @rlubos hinted that may have been due to not having enough buffers / packets.
Definitely seeing things hanging on `mps2_an385`, but adding a `k_msleep()` after connect does not seem to help.
